title: Under the Noon Sun · 2019–2023

pages.message: The natural world plays a critical role in slowing climate change. Every year, about half of human caused carbon dioxide emissions are absorbed by oceans and the world's vegetation, including crops... and trees. Carbon is an element that is in the air, mainly as carbon dioxide. Trees consume this carbon dioxide. They eat it as food and they store it as wood. And 50% of what you see in a tree in a forest is carbon. And that's carbon that if it weren't in the tree, forests were cut down and that wood decomposed, that carbon would end up back in the atmosphere as carbon dioxide.
Brown and dark green represent shorter vegetation. Bright green and white represent taller vegetation.

Carbon dioxide (CO2) is the most prevalent greenhouse gas driving global climate change. However, its increase in the atmosphere would be even more rapid without land and ocean carbon sinks, which collectively absorb about half of human emissions every year.

note: Ours: the Earth turns once under the noon line (the meridian where the Sun stands highest), read a degree of longitude at a time in three bands (north (23, 52), tropics (-23, 23), south (-52, -23)); density is the share of cells with canopy of 10 m or taller. The air is the global CO₂ of each month of the window the map was drawn in (2019-04 to 2023-03), 48 months laid evenly over the turn.

units.lon_deg: degrees east, the middle of the degree the noon line crosses
units.*_height_m: m (mean RH100 of the band's cells with data)
units.*_density: share of the band's cells with data whose canopy is 10 m or taller
units.*_land_share: share of the band's cells with data
units.canopy_height_quarter_degree.png: grey value / 4 = m; 0 = no data; 1440 × 416 cells of 0.25° from 180° W, 52° N
units.xco2_201904-202303_degree.png: grey value / 4 + 380 = ppm XCO2, the mean of the window's 48 months; 360 × 180 cells of 1° from 180° W, 90° N
units.xco2_ppm: ppm (column average, global mean of the month)
